aspects.says: distinct keeps every copy of a class without equals and hashCode, or with equals alone, and the fields in equals decide which copy, the first in encounter order, survives.
basis: section:distinct Uses equals and hashCode, So a Class Without Both Keeps Every Copy

aspects.says: The stream runs the stages in the order written, so an expensive map before a filter runs for every element, and a limit before a filter counts elements the filter drops.
basis: section:A Cheap filter Goes Before an Expensive map, Because map Runs for Every Element That Reaches It

aspects.says: A null returned by flatMap's function is treated as an empty stream, while a null returned by map's function stays in the stream as an element.
basis: section:map Gives One Result per Element; flatMap Splices a Stream per Element into One

aspects.says: map passes on one result per element, so mapping to a list gives a stream of lists; flatMap passes on the elements of the stream each element maps to, zero or more.
basis: section:map Gives One Result per Element; flatMap Splices a Stream per Element into One

aspects.says: limit and skip take the first elements in the stream's encounter order, so paging an unordered source gives different pages from run to run unless it is sorted first, before the skip.
basis: section:limit and skip Count in Encounter Order, and HashSet and Set.of Have None

aspects.says: mapMulti emits zero or more results through a Consumer, and when another call follows it javac needs the result type as a type argument or typed lambda parameters, or the stream becomes a Stream<Object>.
basis: section:mapMulti Emits Zero or More Results Without a Stream per Element, but javac Can't Infer What It Emits

aspects.says: flatMap(Optional::stream) keeps the values of present Optionals and drops the empty ones, where unwrapping with orElse(null) leaves nulls in the stream.
basis: section:map Gives One Result per Element; flatMap Splices a Stream per Element into One

aspects.says: map stays on the kind of stream it is called on; mapToInt enters a primitive stream and mapToObj leaves it, anywhere in a pipeline.
basis: section:map Stays on the Kind of Stream It Was Called On
aspects.reason: the wrong solution (IntStream.map returning a String, or sum() on a Stream<Integer>) doesn't compile, so no graded test can tell a right solution from a wrong one; unit 4.4.2's practice grades the primitive streams themselves

aspects.says: sorted buffers every element before it emits one, so a limit or findFirst after it doesn't stop the source and on an endless stream it never returns.
basis: section:filter and map Pass Each Element On; sorted Holds Every Element Before It Emits One

aspects.says: sorted() on elements that aren't Comparable throws ClassCastException at the terminal operation, and only once two elements are compared.
basis: section:filter and map Pass Each Element On; sorted Holds Every Element Before It Emits One
